ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. Money services businesses are reporting entities under section 5(h) of the Act and must register with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), maintain a compliance program, perform client identification and beneficial ownership verification, conduct ongoing monitoring, file suspicious transaction reports and prescribed transaction reports, and retain records. Federal corporate beneficial-ownership rules are in the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including sections 2.1 and 21.303 to 21.307 concerning individuals with significant control. Quebec corporate beneficial-ownership reporting is governed principally by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, and its implementing regulation; Quebec reporting generally captures an individual who directly or indirectly owns, controls, or has the right to acquire at least 25 percent of voting rights or shares, or who exercises control in fact. The Quebec Money-Services Businesses Act, CQLR c. E-12.000001, requires authorization for money transfer and related prescribed money-services activities. Federal and provincial obligations apply cumulatively where the business is federally incorporated but operates in Quebec.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access for federal corporate individuals-with-significant-control records, subject to statutory access rules; generally public registry disclosure for prescribed Quebec beneficial-owner information through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, with statutory exclusions and confidentiality protections for certain residential and protected information. FINTRAC beneficial-ownership information is not a public registry record.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, licensing, banking, and onboarding, screen all beneficial owners, controllers, directors, officers, authorized signatories, agents, major counterparties, and payment partners against United Nations sanctions, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, applicable Canadian domestic law-enforcement and terrorist-list sources, and OFAC lists where United States nexus, correspondent banking, dollar clearing, or contractual requirements exist. Apply Canadian PEP and head-of-international-organization rules under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds measures, senior-management approval, enhanced monitoring, and documented disposition of potential matches. Screening must cover aliases, transliteration variants, date and place of birth, nationality, adverse media, sanctions evasion, proliferation-financing indicators, high-risk jurisdictions, and payment-rail exposure. A match must be escalated, documented, and cleared by reliable independent evidence; no transaction should proceed while a true sanctions match remains unresolved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services, commonly accessed through the Registraire des entreprises website at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; for a federal corporation, Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre atisedisclosure-service.canada.ca/corporationscanada. A Quebec corporation is formed under the Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1; a federal corporation is formed under the Canada Business Corporations Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec enterprise must comply with Quebec French-language requirements, including the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and applicable regulations. The French name is generally the official corporate name for Quebec business purposes, and a French version or French description may be required. A corporation may use an English or other-language version or an alternate name only where legally permitted and properly declared. Names must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing name or trademark, and must not falsely describe the legal form, business, governmental affiliation, regulated status, or services offered. Foreign-language words and transliterations do not avoid similarity, public-order, or language-law review.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names implying a licensed payment institution, deposit-taking institution, insurer, securities dealer, or government body
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Conduct preliminary searches in the Quebec enterprise register, Corporations Canada database, Canadian trademarks database, domain-name databases, and relevant foreign registries. File the applicable name reservation or incorporation application with the correct jurisdiction and include the proposed French name, alternate name, business description, and supporting consent or regulatory approval for sensitive terms. A Quebec name reservation or accepted name search is subject to the period stated by the Registraire for the applicable filing and is commonly treated as a 90-day reservation period; the filing receipt controls. If rejected, obtain the written deficiency or refusal reason, revise the name or provide evidence of distinctiveness and authorization, and refile. Where a formal administrative decision is issued, request reconsideration or review from the Registraire within the applicable statutory or notice period and preserve proof of filing. A final refusal may be challenged through the applicable Quebec administrative-law remedy, including judicial review before the Superior Court where legally available. Name acceptance does not create trademark rights and does not authorize regulated payment activity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A corporation must maintain a registered office in Quebec if incorporated under Quebec law, or comply with the registered-office and extra-provincial registration rules applicable to a federal corporation carrying on business in Quebec. A commercial virtual office can be acceptable for corporate registration only if it is a genuine service address capable of receiving official notices and maintaining required records. A mailbox-only address, accommodation address, nominee address, or address disconnected from the business is unsuitable. For a cross-border remittance business, virtual-office use is high risk because FINTRAC, Revenu Québec, financial institutions, payment partners, and law-enforcement authorities may require access to records, compliance personnel, transaction controls, customer-support functions, and responsible management. The business should maintain a real Canadian operating address, secure records, documented compliance infrastructure, and personnel proportionate to transaction volume and risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No Canadian statute publishes a general probability of unannounced inspection. Planning assessment: ordinary corporate registration alone has low physical-inspection exposure, but a consumer-remittance MSB has elevated supervisory risk because it is a FINTRAC reporting entity and may require a Quebec money-services-business permit. An estimated 20-40 percent first-cycle review or inspection planning risk is a non-statutory internal estimate for a new high-risk MSB with cross-border rails, not an official government statistic. Risk increases materially with cash pickup, agents, foreign ownership, high-risk corridors, sanctions exposure, unexplained volume, weak records, adverse intelligence, or complaints. The operator must be inspection-ready without advance notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, particularly ss. 7, 10, 11, 12, 14, and 88; Money-Services Businesses Act (Quebec) for the subsequent remittance-service licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) submitted electronically through the REQ online services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. Shares may be issued for nominal consideration. For the money-services business permit, the AMF requires a surety bond or trust account amount set by transaction volume, and FINTRAC registration imposes liquid asset and compliance obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: That the incorporator subscribes for the initial common shares issued in consideration of contributed property valued at CAD 1.00 per share; that the registered office be established at [address], Quebec, with the first director named in the articles accepted; that the following persons be and are appointed as President, Secretary, Treasurer and sole Signing Officer, each to act under the bylaws; and that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, apply for the AMF money-services business permit, register with FINTRAC, and execute all such documents as may be required to carry on the cross-border remittance business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the REQ corporate name database and file a declaration of the proposed name together with the intended business activity. The name must comply with the naming rules of the Quebec Business Corporations Act. Upon approval, a name certificate is issued and remains valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Mandate or power of attorney if filed by an accredited agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Modify the proposed name and re-file; if refused, ask for written reasons and apply to the court for judicial review under section 28 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ – electronic filing (Services en ligne des entreprises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation form using the approved corporate name, set the authorized and issued share capital, appoint the first director(s) with the required consent, provide the head office address and submit electronically. Pay the filing fee online; the certificate of incorporation is issued after the registration is accepted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address REQ's deficiency notice by correcting the Articles and resubmitting within 30 days; unresolved refusals may be contested by judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Revenu Québec (GST/QST and Employer Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the company's enterprise number (NEQ) to open a My Business Account with Revenu Québec. Register for the federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) using Form LM-102-V, and if hiring staff, register as an employer for source deductions, Quebec Parental Insurance Plan (QPIP), and CNESST contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Comply with Revenu Québec's notice to provide missing information within 30 days; any errors in registration are corrected by filing a revised LM-102-V.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Register, Share Certificates and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office; REQ for subsequent annual updating declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the certificate of incorporation from the REQ portal and file it in the corporate minute book. Issue share certificates against the subscribed shares, approve By-Law No. 1, and maintain the register of directors and officers at the registered office. Notify REQ of any changes using the 'Déclaration de mise à jour'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an instrument is defective, call a special board meeting and ratify the corrected document; file any delayed updates with REQ and pay the late-filing penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – Money-Services Business Licensing Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Money-Services Business Permit (permis de société de transfert de fonds) under the Money-Services Businesses Act (Quebec), together with FINTRAC registration as a money services business under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (Canada)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no industrial activity; registration and municipal commercial permit only (no full EIA required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office-based operations; must respect municipal wastewater, recycling and residual materials bylaws; disposal of electronic equipment must comply with the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (Quebec, chapter Q-2, r. 38.1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local municipal fire department for the office premises; electrical installation verification under the Quebec Construction Code; and occupational health and safety clearance from the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) covering workstation ergonomics and emergency evacuation arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC) — national portal: My Business Account (Canada.ca/revenue-agency); for the Province of Quebec: Revenu Québec / Agence du revenu du Québec, through the single-window Registraire des entreprises and CliquezAffaires platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign corporation commencing cross-border money transmission in Canada must: (1) incorporate federally via Corporations Canada or obtain extra-provincial registration in Quebec through the Registraire des entreprises; (2) apply to CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online or Form RC1, activating corporate income tax, GST/HST (RT prefix) and payroll (RP prefix) accounts; (3) register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) number and employer source deductions using the CliquezAffaires single-window service; and (4) where a permanent establishment or taxable Canadian presence exists, appoint a resident agent for service of process and file the federal T2 corporate income tax return and the Quebec CO-17 return. The federal BN and provincial TVQ registrations must be evidenced for FINTRAC money-services-business licensing, banking clearance onboarding and SWIFT correspondent due diligence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; classification follows corporate legal form. Relevant elections and mechanisms: (i) Excise Tax Act (ETA) section 156 election among closely related corporations, deeming intercompany supplies to be zero-rated for GST/HST; (ii) ETA sections 21.1 and 22 elections to zero-rate internal financial services supplied by or to financial institutions, including cross-border payment and remittance rails; (iii) Income Tax Act section 216(4) net-basis election for non-residents deriving Canadian passive income; (iv) ETA section 273 joint-venture election; (v) hybrid-mismatch integrity rules (OECD BEPS Action 2) enacted under the Income Tax Act, which disallow certain deductions rather than providing elective treatment; and (vi) provincial QST elections mirroring federal intercompany elections for Quebec tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered federally by CRA; Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) administered by Revenu Québec; other provincial retail sales tax regimes apply in non-HST provinces.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies over any four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA small-supplier threshold); the Quebec QST registration threshold mirrors this CAD 30,000 quantum. Cross-border remittance services constitute financial services, which are exempt or zero-rated depending on recipient residency, yet a registrant may still require a GST/HST account for exempt or zero-rated financial supplies, payroll, import/export accounts, and to support input tax credit recovery.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transaction reporting or digital stamping regime exists federally or in Quebec. CRA does not mandate transaction-level clearance for GST/HST. Electronic filing is required for GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million; the Pan-Canadian Public Sector E-Invoice standard (Peppol BIS 3.0) is mandatory for suppliers billing the Government of Canada; Revenu Québec requires electronic QST remittance above prescribed thresholds and supports EDI transmission for large enterprises.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act where sold for export and removed from Canada in substantially the same state, evidenced by customs documentation. Services: zero-rated under Schedule VI where supplied to a non-resident who is not a GST/HST registrant and the service is performed wholly or substantially outside Canada. Cross-border remittance and payment transactions qualify as financial services, zero-rated under Part VII of Schedule VI (sections 23–26) where supplied to a non-resident not registered for GST/HST or where the supply relates to a business carried on exclusively outside Canada; supplies of financial services to Canadian residents remain exempt rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA ACI/Cargo Data or B13A Export Declaration) for any physical instruments or goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing removal from Canada
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and underlying export contracts
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/FX contract evidencing foreign-source settlement
Non-resident recipient identification and supporting transaction documentation for zero-rated financial services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit focus includes absence of export evidence, round-tripped funds, related-party non-resident recipients, and artificially structured zero-rating claims. The normal four-year GST/HST reassessment window is extended indefinitely where a registrant has made misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default or fraud. Civil penalties include late-filing penalties under ETA section 280, false-statement penalties under ETA section 285 (including a 50% gross-negligence penalty on the net tax that was sought to be avoided), and criminal prosecution under ETA section 239 for wilful evasion, carrying fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Revenu Québec imposes parallel QST penalties and prescribed-rate interest, with retrospective clawback of wrongfully zero-rated refunds plus compound interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank; OSFI supervises federally regulated banks; FINTRAC administers Canada's AML/CFT regime; Global Affairs Canada administers economic sanctions; Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility as an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction. No general exchange-control approval is needed for investment, dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or branch remittances. Practical hurdles are limited to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax, treaty-reduced withholding documentation, transfer-pricing and attribution audits by CRA, sanctions screening, and Quebec provincial measures applicable to non-resident payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold foreign currency, sell it in the spot market, or apply it against import costs. The only binding duties are documentary retention for CRA audit, Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting, and FINTRAC reporting for any electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium, only through a FINTRAC-registered Canadian money services business (MSB) branch, agent, or partnership. UK/EU EMI licences do not passport into Canada, cannot clear CAD directly, and cannot access Canadian payment systems without a Payments Canada participant. Foreign fintechs can support origination, FX quotation and client interface, but the Canadian legal entity must hold a FINTRAC MSB registration, appoint a Canadian AML compliance officer, and lodge sanctions and transaction-monitoring protocols acceptable to a tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For high-risk cross-border remittance entities, Canadian banks normally require at least one director and one ultimate beneficial owner or senior authorized signatory to perform identity verification in person at a Canadian branch or before a bank-approved notary or lawyer in Quebec. Fully remote onboarding is possible only after preliminary enhanced due diligence and a bank-approved live video interview; it is not guaranteed for high-risk business models. A physical Quebec registered office, local compliance officer, and corporate records at the Registraire des entreprises materially raise approval odds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex corporate ownership layers, nominee directors, or unclear ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate register and Register of Directors; notarized UBO attestation; shareholding diagram; Registraire des entreprises attestation and NEQ; tax clearance from Revenu Québec; audited financial statements; previous bank reference letters; written acknowledgment that no bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk classification for cross-border remittance and money transmission activities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive written AML/CFT and KYC program; completed enterprise-wide risk assessment; appointment of designated AML compliance officer; FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation; transaction-monitoring and suspicious-transaction escalation procedures; staff training records; clear remittance-corridor policy with source-and-use-of-funds maps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, OFAC/FATF adverse-media hits on shareholders, counterparties, or beneficiary countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening results; negative media and open-source search screenshots; certification that all directors, UBOs, and counterparties are not designated persons; legal opinion on applicable Canadian sanctions; end-use and origin-of-funds declarations; contractual prohibition against dealing with sanctioned parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound capital injection, large shareholder loans, or third-party settlement flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution approving the capital injection; executed subscription or loan agreement; source-of-wealth evidence; sworn declaration of beneficial owner; no-third-party-settlement policy; transaction-level invoice and contract support; board minutes explaining economic purpose; CRA and Revenu Québec filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient substance in Quebec: no office, no staff, no local compliance function
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or property ownership in Quebec; notarial deed for registered office; employment contracts and organization chart; Quebec GST/QST registrations and payroll program account; board minutes showing local management decisions; insurance certificate including professional liability and bond; FINTRAC MSB registration showing Quebec as principal place of business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or subordinated-debt injections are effected through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messages to the Canadian account in CAD. Canada uses bank transit numbers plus account numbers, not IBAN. Field 70 narrative should clearly state 'Capital injection under investment agreement dated [date], entity NEQ number, non-resident investor name'. Inbound wires in foreign currency may be converted at a Canadian bank at market rates; no exchange-control authorization is required. The bank must verify the incoming beneficial owner, conduct sanctions screening, and file a FINTRAC EFT report for amounts equal to or above CAD 10,000. Document packages should include board resolutions, subscription agreement or loan note, UBO declarations, audited or management financial statements, and Investment Canada Act notification if the non-Canadian investor crosses review thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments are cleared via: SWIFT MT103 for direct invoice settlements and remittance payouts, with field 70 referencing invoice or PO number and Incoterms; documentary letters of credit via MT700 and MT707 plus presentation through a Quebec advising bank for freight and commodity settlements; SWIFT MT202 for interbank liquidity; Payments Canada Lynx for large-value CAD transfers; Real-Time Rail for low-value immediate CAD payments; and Fedwire, CHIPS, or cross-border ACH for USD payables through the Canadian bank's US correspondent. Each bank retains records for at least five years under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX swaps and rollovers for liquidity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps in CAD/USD and CAD/EUR
Foreign exchange options on freely convertible currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-convertible or restricted secondary currencies where no onshore deliverable market exists for the relevant exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the incorporation or enterprise registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal default notice; administrative strike-off if not remedied within 30 days; penal fine up to CAD 2,000 for the legal person

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; tax balance payable 2 months after year-end (4 months for eligible CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% of unpaid balance, plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; compounded daily interest; statutory director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; tax balance payable 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs with Quebec small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% of unpaid balance, increasing 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on arrears; administrative penalty on unreported revenue

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and QST Annual Return (annual filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for GST/HST; Revenu Québec for QST
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; acceleration to quarterly or monthly basis if reporting threshold exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty 5% plus 1% per month (max 12%); overdue interest; false statement penalties up to 50% of additional tax assessed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the registration anniversary date; FINTRAC sends renewal notice approximately 60 days in advance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalty up to CAD 500,000 for corporations; suspension or loss of registration; criminal fine up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment for operating unregistered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as determined by AMF licence cycle, typically prior to expiry anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Licence suspension or revocation; Administrative monetary penalty; prohibition on operating money transfer business in Québec; personal liability for unauthorized activity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Québec Business Corporations Act, a non-distributing private corporation is exempt from a mandatory audit unless shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares make a written request; mandatory audit required for distributing corporations and for regulated money-services licensees where AMF or FINTRAC imposes audited financial statements as a licence condition
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public or distributing enterprises and for regulated financial institutions where prescribed; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) permitted for private corporations unless regulatory directive requires IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: QBCA requires maintenance of a Register of Individuals with Significant Control at the registered office; any share transfer or change creating, modifying, or terminating significant control must be recorded within 15 days of knowledge; the annual declaration to REQ must include an attestation that the register is complete and up to date; directors and officers are personally liable for failing to keep or update the register or making false attestations
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minutes of Proceedings and Resolutions (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 25,000 per year depending on size, complexity, and regulatory scope
